value.body: A strength and conditioning (S&C) coach prepares athletes physically for their sport, building strength, speed, endurance and mobility while lowering injury risk. Sports academies, professional teams, schools with sports programmes and performance gyms hire for this work. A typical day involves running training sessions, testing athletes and adjusting programmes with the sports coach and physiotherapist.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BPES / B.P.Ed or B.Sc Sports Science

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Free weights, fitness-testing equipment, training logs

items.label: Certification
items.value: S&C certifications are often asked for alongside the degree

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often start as assistant S&C coaches at academies or as trainers in performance gyms, building hours with athletes. A recognised strength and conditioning certification and practical coaching experience strengthen applications.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Working within a coach and physio team

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: head S&C coach, sports scientist, high-performance manager.
Early-morning and evening sessions and team travel are common.
Overlaps with fitness training, but focused on athletes rather than general clients.

value.title: UG students in Physical Education
value.note: All years of the course; most graduates go into teaching or coaching broadly, not only S&C. Counts only institutions that responded to AISHE, so national totals may be higher.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24 (Table 12, UG enrolment by subject)
